stem: On what date was the **United Nations** founded?

options.rationale: This is when the OAU was founded.
This is when Zimbabwe became independent and soon joined the UN.
This is the date of UDI.

explanation: The UN was founded on 24 October 1945.

stem: Which UN agency works mainly for **children**?

options.rationale: UNESCO deals with education, science and culture.

explanation: UNICEF: the United Nations Children's Fund.

stem: Which UN agency lists sites such as **Great Zimbabwe** as World Heritage Sites?
explanation: UNESCO (education, science and culture) runs the World Heritage list.

stem: What was the main idea of **non-alignment**?

options.content: Joining the Western bloc led by the USA
Joining the Eastern bloc led by the Soviet Union
Forming one government for all of Africa
Not joining either bloc in the Cold War

explanation: NAM members stayed independent of the rival power blocs.

stem: Which UN organ has **five permanent members** with a veto?

options.rationale: All members have one vote each; there is no veto.
This is a court of judges.
This is the administration, led by the Secretary-General.

explanation: China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States hold permanent seats with a veto.

stem: After a drought near Gwanda, families receive maize meal, beans and cooking oil from a UN agency. Which agency is this **most likely** to be?

options.rationale: UNESCO deals with education and culture.
The court settles disputes between states.

explanation: WFP provides food aid in droughts and disasters.

stem: Why do many African states call for **reform of the Security Council**?

options.content: The Council has too many African permanent members already
The Council never meets to discuss peace and security
The General Assembly has a veto that blocks the Council
options.rationale: The General Assembly has no veto.

options.content: Africa has no permanent seat on the Council
options.rationale: Correct: yet many issues before it concern Africa.

explanation: Africa has elected seats only, so many African states argue for permanent representation.

stem: Which statement **best** describes the relationship between UN agencies and the government of Zimbabwe?

options.content: Agencies govern the provinces where they have offices
The government must obey every request made by an agency
Agencies support national programmes but do not replace the government
Agencies may only work in countries with no government

explanation: Agencies work with and through national institutions.
hints: Who is responsible for national services?

stem: Harare hosted the summit of the Non-Aligned Movement in 1986.
The UN applied sanctions to Rhodesia after UDI.
explanation: True. The UN supported the right of colonial peoples to self-determination.

stem: Match each UN agency with an example of its work in Zimbabwe.

right.content: Immunising children and supporting child protection
Listing Mana Pools as a World Heritage Site

explanation: Each agency works in its own field.

payload.template: The UN is led by the Secretary-{{blank:a}}. The International Court of Justice sits in {{blank:b}}.

explanation: The Secretary-General leads the Secretariat; the ICJ sits in The Hague.

stem: In which year was the Non-Aligned Movement founded?
explanation: NAM was founded in **1961** in Belgrade.

stem: State **four** aims of the United Nations.

points.description: Maintain international peace and security
Develop friendly relations among nations
Solve economic, social and humanitarian problems through cooperation
Promote human rights / be a centre for coordinating nations' actions

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: To keep world peace and security, to develop friendly relations among nations, to cooperate in solving economic, social and humanitarian problems, and to promote human rights.

stem: Explain **two** benefits Zimbabwe gains from membership of the UN.

points.description: Humanitarian help
Developed: e.g. WFP food aid after droughts and Cyclone Idai
Health and child-welfare programmes / World Heritage recognition / a voice in world affairs
Developed: e.g. UNICEF immunisation; UNESCO listing attracts tourists

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Zimbabwe receives humanitarian help, for example food aid from WFP after droughts and Cyclone Idai. It also benefits from health and child-welfare programmes, such as UNICEF's support for immunisation, which protects children from disease.

hints: Give the benefit and an example.

stem: Explain **three** reasons why newly independent countries joined the Non-Aligned Movement.

points.description: To keep their independence
Developed: avoid being controlled by either Cold War bloc
To oppose colonialism and apartheid
Developed: support liberation in southern Africa and elsewhere
To gain a stronger collective voice / economic cooperation
Developed: together they could press for fairer trade and development

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Newly independent countries wanted to keep their independence and avoid being controlled by either Cold War bloc. They also wanted to oppose colonialism and apartheid, supporting liberation movements such as those in southern Africa. Together they had a stronger voice, which they used to press for fairer trade and more development.

hints: Think about independence, liberation and a shared voice.

stem:
**Source A** — a poster (described in words) of the kind displayed at a district hospital (described in words; invented for this question)

> The poster shows a nurse vaccinating a baby held by her mother. Along the top are the words "Every child, every vaccine". At the bottom are the logos of the Ministry of Health and Child Care and of two UN agencies, one for children and one for health. A line of small print says that the vaccines are free at all public clinics.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which two UN agencies are **most likely** shown on the poster?

options.rationale: These deal with culture and food.
WFP deals with food, not health.
UNESCO deals with education and culture.

parts.explanation: UNICEF works for children and WHO for health.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: The poster suggests that UN agencies work together with the national government.
parts.explanation: True: the Ministry's logo appears beside the agencies'.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain **two** reasons why child immunisation is important to Zimbabwe.

points.description: Protects children from deadly diseases
Developed: fewer child deaths and disabilities
Prevents outbreaks / saves money
Developed: protects the whole community; treating disease costs more than preventing it

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Immunisation protects children from serious diseases such as measles and polio, reducing child deaths and disability. It also prevents outbreaks that could spread through the community, and preventing disease costs far less than treating it.

explanation: Reading a described poster about UN cooperation in health.
hints: Think about the logos and the message.

stem: Answer the questions on Zimbabwe and the United Nations.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Describe **two** main organs of the United Nations.

points.description: General Assembly: all members, one vote each
discusses world issues and approves the budget
Security Council: 15 members, five permanent with a veto
responsible for peace and security

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The General Assembly includes all member states, each with one vote; it discusses world issues and approves the UN budget. The Security Council has 15 members, five of them permanent with a veto, and is responsible for international peace and security.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: "Zimbabwe gains more from the UN than it gives." How far do you agree?

points.description: For: food aid, immunisation, disease control, World Heritage status, a voice in world affairs
Against / balance: Zimbabwe pays contributions, contributes to peacekeeping, must implement conventions and report
Limits: influence over major decisions is limited by the veto; programmes depend on donor funding
Supported judgement

levels.descriptor: Developed explanation of several relevant points or arguments, supported by accurate, specific knowledge and examples, considering more than one side and reaching a supported judgement that answers the question.
Developed explanation of some factors or arguments with relevant supporting detail; a judgement is attempted but is only partly supported, or the other side is thin.
Some explanation of one or two relevant factors, or several points described with limited explanation; little or no judgement.
Simple, general or narrative statements with limited relevance to the question; little explanation.

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
Zimbabwe gains a great deal from the UN. WFP has provided food aid after droughts and Cyclone Idai, UNICEF and WHO support immunisation and disease control, and UNESCO's World Heritage listing of sites such as Great Zimbabwe brings recognition and tourism. Zimbabwe also has a voice in the General Assembly.

Zimbabwe also gives. It pays its contributions, has contributed to peacekeeping and must implement and report on conventions such as the Convention on the Rights of the Child. Its influence over major decisions is limited, because the permanent members hold a veto.

I largely agree: the practical benefits in health, food security and heritage are greater than the costs, even though Zimbabwe's influence is limited.

explanation: Describing UN organs and evaluating Zimbabwe's membership.
